query: Why do some incidents take longer to resolve?

per_column.name: incident_type
per_column.rationale: Categorizing incidents by type gives a strong grouping axis to compare resolution times across problem classes. Values are soundly derived from short_description ('VPN'->connectivity, 'database'->database, 'Email'->email).

per_column.name: incident_recurrence
per_column.rationale: Whether an incident is recurring could plausibly correlate with resolution time, so it has analytical leverage. But the source text (a single short_description) does not support a recurrence determination; every sampled row is labeled 'True' with no textual basis, indicating invented values.

per_column.name: incident_scope
per_column.rationale: Scope (individual vs department vs infrastructure-wide) is a meaningful axis for explaining resolution effort. Some values are grounded ('sales department'->department_wide), but 'individual_user' for 'VPN connection issue' and 'infrastructure_wide' as dominant value are often inferred beyond what silent descriptions state; still mostly a warranted reading.

per_column.name: description_clarity
per_column.rationale: Clarity of the ticket description plausibly affects triage/resolution time, a reasonable new axis. The generic/specific/vague categorization is a defensible reading of the description text, though somewhat subjective.

per_column.name: assigned_technician
per_column.rationale: Assignee could matter for resolution time, but this is essentially redundant with the existing 'assigned_to'/'closed_by' columns. Moreover the row samples contain no technician information in the source text, so specific names appear invented/unsupported.

per_column.name: closure_status
per_column.rationale: A boolean closed/not-closed flag is largely redundant with the existing 'state'/'closed_at' columns and near-constant (421 true), offering little analytical leverage for this query. Values are well grounded in closed_at presence.

judge.rationale: The set offers several genuinely useful new axes (incident_type, incident_scope, description_clarity) for explaining resolution-time variation. However incident_recurrence and assigned_technician show unsupported/invented values not derivable from the single-line descriptions, and assigned_technician/closure_status are largely redundant with existing original columns. Overall moderately useful with notable groundedness concerns on two columns.
